source_snapshot.message:
feat(mcp): add `ix mcp install` and `ix mcp doctor`

Registers `ix mcp` with the AI clients present on the machine, and reports
what each one currently points at. Covers Claude Code, Codex, Cursor,
VS Code, Gemini CLI, OpenClaw and opencode.

Writes go through each client's own MCP command wherever one exists
(claude/codex/gemini `mcp add`, `openclaw mcp set`, `code --add-mcp`), so
the client owns its config format and an upstream format change cannot
corrupt a file here. Only Cursor (no MCP CLI) and opencode (`opencode mcp
add` is interactive and takes no arguments) are written directly; both are
JSON, merged in place with every existing key preserved and a `.bak` kept.
A config that does not parse is refused rather than replaced.

install never overwrites. Ix already ships six per-host plugins that
register their own server under the same name — `ix-memory` currently
resolves to `python3 .../server.py` on Codex and a Gemini extension's
`node dist/server.js` on this machine — so a name held by anything that is
not `ix mcp` is reported and left alone. --force replaces it, --host
narrows the run, --dry-run writes nothing. A registration that cannot be
read is treated as occupied, not free: guessing "free" is the one wrong
guess that destroys someone's config.

Two things detection has to get right, both found against real installs:

- Gemini prints its listing to stderr behind ~28 extension-loader errors,
  several naming the extension, which is itself called ix-memory. Matching
  the first line containing the name reports a diagnostic as the
  registration, so obvious log lines are skipped.
- `openclaw mcp list` prints names only, and `openclaw mcp show`
  pretty-prints JSON across lines, putting "ix" and "mcp" on different
  ones. Line-at-a-time matching read our own entry as a stranger's and
  raised a false conflict on every re-run; definitions are now classified
  whole.

doctor additionally checks that the bare command `ix` resolves on PATH,
since that is what every registration launches.
